sentences.text: This animal possessed a neck that was proportionally long, containing at least 38 vertebrae in the neck region.
A unique feature of this species includes small, cone-shaped bumps on the front parts of its neck joints.
Scientists consider this creature one of the earliest known plesiosaurs in the fossil record.
Its name combines the Greek word for dawn with the name of a famous earlier sea reptile.
Researchers have found only one complete skeleton, which serves as the primary example for the species.
This specimen was gathered from the Blue Lias Formation near Watchet in Somerset.
The genus was formally named by Benson, Evans, and Druckenmiller in the year 2012.
An initial study in 2012 suggested it was the most primitive member of the plesiosauroid group.
However, a subsequent analysis by the same authors in 2014 placed it outside that specific group.
This animal lived between 199.6 and 198 million years ago during the earliest Hettangian stage.
Other records place its time range within the Hettangian stage from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
